heading: Extension of Code to extra-territorial offences.
text:
The provisions of this Code apply also to any offence committed by—
[10][(1) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India;
(2) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be.]
[11][(3) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer resource located in India.]
[12][Explanation.—In this section—
(a) the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, if committed in
India, would be punishable under this Code; in—
Pargana Dhalbhum and the Kolhan in the District of Singhbum—see Gazette of India, 1881, Pt. I, p. 504.
It has been extended under s. 5 of the same Act to the Lushai Hills—see Gazette of India, 1898, Pt. II, p. 345.
(b) the expression “computer resource” shall have the meaning assigned to it in clause (k) of
sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 (21 of 2000).]
[1][Illustration]
[2]***A, [3][who is [4][a citizen of India]], commits a murder in Uganda. He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in [5][India] in which he may be found.
[6]* * * * *
status_note: The Act is repealed. Kept in India Code's 'Repeal Acts' collection; record title reads 'The Indian Penal Code, 45 of 1860 (Rep., Act 45 of 2023)' (read 2026-11-21)
